title: The Field Inside Four Borders

script.text: This field was India, inside Bangladesh, inside India, inside Bangladesh.
It sat here, in the far north of Bangladesh.

script: Inside it, a pocket of India.
Inside that, a pocket of Bangladesh.

script.text: And inside that, one last scrap of India: Dahala Khagrabari.
The only third-order enclave in the world.

script: It was a single jute field, owned by a farmer from the Bangladeshi pocket around it.
And it wasn't alone. Nearly [200|two hundred] pockets of one country sat stranded inside the other.

script.text: More than [50,000|fifty thousand] people lived in them.
In [1974|nineteen seventy-four], the two countries agreed to swap them. It took [41|forty-one] more years.
At midnight on the last day of July [2015|twenty fifteen], [162|a hundred and sixty-two] enclaves changed hands at once.

script: The Indian field became plain Bangladesh.
Today, it's just a field again. Inside nothing at all.
